page.layout: One page of text, single column. Woodcut ornament at the head; then headings, verse epigrams with a large initial, a horizontal rule, a further heading and epigram, and a signature line at the foot. No margin notes.

l.i: Et non ex isto corpore casta fugit!

main_text.l: SI fuit ille tibi, Lucretia, gratus adulter,
Immerito ex merita præmia morte petis.
Sin potius casto vis est allata pudori,
Quis furor alterius crimine velle mori?
Frustra igitur laudem captas, Lucretia. Nâque
Vel sce lerata cadis, vel furiosa ruis.
POst Persas fusos quæsitasque orbis habenas,
Armis non potui cedere, cedo dolis.

page.notes: The first verse line of LVCRETIA is printed in mixed roman and italic; the large initials D and P are woodcut letters, read as D and P. Some words of the epigram text are uncertain and copied as printed; the line "Et non ex isto corpore casta fugit!" is italic. The top ornament and the horizontal rule are not text.
